key_insight: Flexible, modular robots can move and manipulate objects individually, then physically connect into task-adaptive forms. This lets them cooperate to carry objects, cross gaps and navigate difficult terrain.
problem_solved: Fixed robot shapes can limit versatility across tasks. This work addresses the challenge of combining mobility, object manipulation and physical cooperation in adaptable robotic units.
method: Use flexible tensegrity continuum robot modules that combine locomotion and manipulation in a single unit.
Physically connect modules to form cooperative structures suited to different tasks.
Demonstrate collaborative object transport, gap crossing and navigation through challenging terrain.
impact: For embodied AI and robotics practitioners, the work highlights robot morphology as an additional dimension of task adaptation. It motivates learning and control approaches that coordinate both individual movement and collective configuration.
visual_elements: Labeled module diagram highlighting its flexible structure and movement/manipulation capabilities.
Sequence showing separate robot modules connecting into a task-adaptive form.
Three-panel task illustration: carrying an object, crossing a gap and traversing rough terrain.
Concept diagram linking task requirements to different cooperative configurations.
paper_title: Tensegrity continuum robots enable task-adaptive morphologies for cooperative behaviours
paper_authors: Mahmud Hasan Saikot, Sydney Spiegel, Sudheera Akalanka Kariyawasam, Andrew Stefka, Josh Chrisler
